```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidymodels)
library(tidytext)
library(keras)
library(tensorflow)
library(tokenizers)
```

```{r}
load("../../data/claims-raw.RData")
```

```{r}
# uses preliminary 1&2 in order to get the validation set
# just renames it to validation for clearer use 
# uses similar code to how they get train_y to get the validation_y

validation <- holdout
validation_y <- labels(holdout_ids)
```

```{r}
# calculates the tf-idf values for our training partitioned data
claims_tf_idf <- heading_tokens %>% 
  filter(.id %in% train$.id) %>% 
  count(.id, term) %>%
  bind_tf_idf(term = term,
              document = .id,
              n = n)

train_df <- claims_tf_idf %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = .id,
              names_from = term,
              values_from = tf_idf,
              values_fill = 0)
```

```{r}
# calculates the tf-idf values for our validation data
# uses the idf results from training

validation_df <- heading_tokens %>%
  
  # calculates the tf values
  filter(.id %in% validation$.id) %>%
  count(.id, term) %>% 
  group_by(.id) %>%
  mutate(tf_2 = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # we only want to use words that are also in our training data
  inner_join(claims_tf_idf %>% 
              group_by(term) %>%
              slice_head(n=1) %>%
              select(term, idf),
            by = "term") %>%
  
  # calculates the tf_idf values 
  mutate(tf_idf = tf_2 * idf) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = .id,
              names_from = term,
              values_from = tf_idf,
              values_fill = 0)
```

```{r}
# ensures that our validation df has the same tokens as training
# for all of the tokens not in validation, we add in 0 for their values
missing_colnames <- colnames(train_df)[
  !(colnames(train_df) %in% colnames(validation_df))]

missing_cols <- matrix(rep(0, length(missing_colnames) * nrow(validation_df)), 
                 nrow = nrow(validation_df), ncol = length(missing_colnames))

colnames(missing_cols) <- missing_colnames

# adds in our missing tokens
# changes the order of columns in order to match our train_df
validation_df <- bind_cols(validation_df, missing_cols)
validation_df <- validation_df[, colnames(train_df)]
```

```{r}
#there are some missing id columns, so we need to add them back
print(length(train_y) == length(train_df$.id))
print(length(validation_y) == length(validation_df$.id))
```

```{r}
# left joins with our original validation and training data 
# replaces all NA values with 0
# adds back our missing id columns

train_df <- train %>% 
  select(.id) %>%
  left_join(train_df, by = ".id")

train_df[is.na(train_df)] <- 0

validation_df <- validation %>%
  select(.id) %>%
  left_join(validation_df, by = ".id")

validation_df[is.na(validation_df)] <- 0
```


```{r}
# we already have train_y and validation_y from the preliminary 1&2
# we just need to extract the training predictors
# remove the id column since it's just an identifier

train_x <- train_df %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.id) %>%
  as.matrix()

validation_x <- validation_df %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.id) %>%
  as.matrix()
```

```{r}
set_random_seed(197)

# specifies that we want a feedforward network model
nn_model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(train_x))

# adds a hidden layer with 10 units and a hyperbolic tangent activation function
# uses a sigmoid activation function for our output layer
nn_model <- nn_model %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 10, activation = "tanh") %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 1, activation = "sigmoid") 

summary(nn_model)
```

```{r}
set_random_seed(197)

# uses a binary cross-entropy loss function 
# uses stochastic gradient descent
# measures our binary accuracy
nn_model <- nn_model %>%
  compile(loss = "binary_crossentropy",
          optimizer = tf$keras$optimizers$legacy$SGD(),
          metrics = "binary_accuracy")

# fits the model to our training data
# uses fitted model to make predictions on our validation data after each epoch
claims_mod <- nn_model %>%
  fit(x = train_x, 
      y = train_y, 
      epochs = 200,
      validation_data = list(validation_x, validation_y))

# graphs the loss and binary accuracy across epochs
plot(claims_mod)
```

```{r}
# results of our model on the training data

train_eval <- evaluate(nn_model, train_x, train_y)
train_eval
```

```{r}
# results of the model on our validation data
# the neural network validation has approxiamtely 4% higher accuracy

validation_eval <- evaluate(nn_model, validation_x, validation_y)
validation_eval
```
